# Nightjar Press

This is our two-ink proof desk. A printer checks the pass order and selects a plate before mixing ink. The original job shown here is a sample. Keep the Nightjar Press name, the plum work surface and our two spot inks. Marigold appears in both the press signature and plate A. Iris identifies plate B in the chart and key. In the mixing controls, a marigold fill always means “selected”, whichever radio is checked; the native radio dot and label identify the plate. The chart and its key must agree in both colour and shape. Keep the revision notice beside the job. It affects which proof the printer can use.

Use system sans for work labels and Georgia for the job title. Keep the composition bold, the action labels short and the job information in reading order.
